sections.h2: Ways to sell in Palm Coast
sections.html:
An owner in Palm Coast can take a cash offer, list with an agent, or sell as is. Many homes here draw interest for canal frontage, trails and a retiree-friendly layout.

The city covers 95.36 square miles of land, so conditions differ by neighborhood. Canal homes, trail-side homes and newer subdivisions each draw different buyers. A seller who knows which group fits the property can choose between a canal-focused listing and a quick sale to someone who handles the repairs. The city has 39,807 households with an average of 2.46 people, so buyers are often couples or small families.

Palm Coast is a young city on Florida's northeast coast, incorporated in 1999. It has 70 miles of saltwater and freshwater canals, the Intracoastal Waterway and more than 130 miles of connecting trails. Water access is what many buyers look for first, so describe it clearly in your listing.

Useful numbers: Building Services at 386-986-3780 and Code Compliance at 386-986-3764. The city's Departments menu includes a lien request form and a garage sale permit page, both handy for a seller clearing out a house. City Council meets on the first Tuesday of each month at 6:00 p.m. and the third Tuesday at 9 a.m., at City Hall, 160 Lake Avenue.

Growth here has been fast and retirees make up a large share of residents. The 2020 count was 89,258 people, up from 75,180 in 2010.

More work needs a permit than many owners assume. Florida Building Code section 105.1 covers construction, alterations, repairs, re-roofs and work on electrical, gas, mechanical and plumbing systems.

  • Pergolas, gazebos, decks, detached patio covers and greenhouses are residential accessory structures and need a permit.
  • The city uses a design wind speed of 120 miles per hour, and a pre-manufactured structure must be engineered for that figure.
  • Applications go through the online permit portal, and accessory structure review is usually done in 3 to 5 business days.
  • A permit stays active six months from issue. If it lapses without the required inspections, a new permit is required.
  • A foundation survey may be required before vertical construction.

If you added a deck or screened structure, confirm the permit was closed out. A buyer's inspector or the title company may flag the gap, and it is easier to fix before you list.

The Flagler County Property Appraiser sets value each January 1, and the Flagler County Tax Collector bills in November. If you held title on January 1, that year's bill is yours, and it is usually split with the buyer at closing.

  • Homestead filing closes March 1. The first $25,000 of the exemption reaches all taxes, and up to $25,000 more reduces non-school taxes on value over $50,000.
  • A paid-in-full discount of 4 percent applies in November and shrinks to 1 percent by February.
  • Non-homestead assessments cannot rise more than 10 percent a year.
  • Unpaid bills go delinquent April 1.

Call the county property appraiser for current exemption details.

Deed stamps run $0.70 on each $100 of price, the state rate, and the clerk collects them as the deed is filed. Clerk charges come on top: $5.00 on page one, $4.00 for every added page, $1.00 per name beyond four, plus a $4 per page technology charge.

A quitclaim deed is taxable too. A Department of Revenue advisement found that a lady bird deed on the facts presented transferred no present beneficial interest and drew no stamp tax. Your closing agent will total the real figures.

Start with the clerk's probate file. About 29.5% of residents are 65 or older, so estate sales are a regular part of this market. Summary administration fits non-exempt assets of $150,000 or less, or a death over two years ago. Creditor claims are barred after the later of three months from first notice publication or thirty days from service on a required creditor.

To remove an occupant who has no permission, Florida's sheriff process asks for a verified complaint and conditions such as no tenancy, no family tie and no pending lawsuit. A claim of adverse possession needs seven years of possession plus tax payments and a return filed with the property appraiser, and living in a home on that claim before filing is trespass. A month-to-month tenant, by contrast, gets 30 days' notice before a monthly period ends.

• Permit records: call Building Services at 386-986-3780 and confirm that decks, pergolas, roofs and screened structures were closed out. A permit lapses after six months without inspections.
  • City liens and code issues: use the lien request form in the Departments menu, and reach Code Compliance at 386-986-3764.
  • Utility account: the Customer Service line, 386-986-2360, handles billing and new service, so schedule the change for closing day.
  • Garage sale: the city has a garage sales page if you plan to clear out belongings before moving.
  • Homestead paperwork: keep your exemption records so you can use portability if you buy another Florida home within three years.

None of this has to be finished before a cash offer, but each item shortens the time between a signed contract and the closing table.

After you sign, the title company searches the record for liens and unpaid taxes, and the closing agent prepares the deed and the settlement statement. In a cash sale there is no lender appraisal, so the date is mostly set by title work and any open permit or lien. Keep your phone on during that stretch, because a missing document is the usual reason a closing slips.

faqs.q: When did Palm Coast become a city?
faqs.a: It incorporated in 1999. It sits along canals and the Intracoastal Waterway in Flagler County.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit for a deck or pergola?
faqs.a: Yes. Pergolas, gazebos, decks and detached patio covers are accessory structures that require a permit under the Florida Building Code.

faqs.q: What wind speed does the city use for design?
faqs.a: 120 miles per hour. A pre-manufactured structure should carry a Florida engineer's signed and sealed plans for that speed before you buy it.

faqs.q: How long does a Palm Coast building permit stay active?
faqs.a: Six months from issue. If it expires without the required inspections, a new permit is needed.

faqs.q: What is the deed stamp rate in Flagler County?
faqs.a: $0.70 per $100 of price, collected by the clerk as the deed is filed.
